note: Shared redaction vectors. CLAUDE.md: a rule implemented in both JavaScript and Python gets ONE fixture that both implementations run. Before this file existed they were pinned by two DISJOINT hand-written lists, every vector in each carrying exactly one '@' -- so D-SINK-1 (a password tail surviving into the host position when the password contains an un-encoded '@') was invisible to both. The two renderings differ on purpose: the helper emits scheme://host, Model emits the bare host. So a vector pins the PROPERTY, not the formatting: the host must appear, and no fragment listed in mustNotAppear may.
credentialsAreFake: Every credential here is invented and every host is under the reserved .test TLD. Never put a real provider value in this file.

vectors.why: the ordinary case both suites already had
D-SINK-1: an un-encoded '@' inside the password
two '@' and no password, which is still userinfo
credentials in the query string, the Xtream shape
credentials in the path, the other Xtream shape
no userinfo at all must survive unharmed
two URLs in one line, the second carrying the doubled '@'
an unknown scheme is still a URL and still redacts
